section_summary: The concluding pages of a report describe falling exports and rising costs in Japan’s glassware, thermos, hat, and handkerchief industries in 1937–1938. They also discuss wartime labor obligations, tariffs, and manufacturers’ complaints about government policy. Two document file notes cross-reference a 1938 industrial review and a 1937 memorandum on munitions production in the Nagasaki Consular District.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: Sender of the despatch referenced in the document file note

people.name: Bruner
people.role: Associated with the State Department memorandum referenced in the document file note

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese industrial conditions, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Reports production costs, export declines, tariffs, and wartime pressures affecting several Japanese consumer industries.
subfiles.summary: The report concludes its discussion of glassware exports, then surveys the thermos, hat, and handkerchief industries. It records higher material costs, interrupted production, falling exports, and the effects of the China conflict and Manchukuo tariffs. An Osaka industry representative criticizes uncertain government policy. The final page carries forwarding instructions for copies.

subfiles.title: Document file note for despatch no. 3155
subfiles.about: Cross-references a despatch transmitting the Japan Advertiser annual review of Japanese financial and industrial matters.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch no. 3155 and its statistical annual review for July 1937 through June 1938.

subfiles.title: Document file note for memorandum on munitions industries
subfiles.about: Cross-references a memorandum on munitions industries and military stores in the Nagasaki Consular District.
subfiles.summary: Points to a memorandum on munitions production and military stores for national defense mobilization.
